sentiment.rationale: Forward guidance was effectively reduced relative to the company's own prior trajectory: the Q1 revenue guide of $43B implies ~65% YoY growth, a sharp deceleration from the 114% full-year growth just reported. Gross margin is guided to a trough of 71% (down from 73.5% reported), with a back-loaded, unproven recovery to mid-70s later in the fiscal year. Management explicitly flagged tariffs as an 'unknown' and China export controls as a persistent cap. The strong backward-looking beat ($11B Blackwell ramp) is offset by these forward-looking headwinds, resulting in a negative score.

summary.revenue: Q4 revenue of $39.3 billion, up 12% sequentially and 78% year on year. Full-year fiscal 2025 revenue was $130.5 billion, up 114% from the prior year.
summary.guidance: Q1 revenue expected to be $43 billion, plus or minus 2%. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins expected to be 70.6% and 71%, respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points. Full-year fiscal 2026 operating expenses expected to grow in the mid-30s.
summary.margin: Q4 non-GAAP gross margin 73.5%, down sequentially. Q1 non-GAAP gross margin guided to 71% (±50bp). Management expects gross margin to return to the mid-70s late this fiscal year when Blackwell is fully ramped.
key_risks: Gross margin trough during Blackwell ramp, with a back-loaded recovery path requiring ~200bp improvement per quarter in H2.
Tariffs explicitly described as 'a little bit of an unknown' with no quantification of timing, scope, or magnitude.
China data center sales remain capped at about half of pre-export-control levels, with no improvement expected absent regulatory change.
Networking revenue declined 3% sequentially during the product transition, though expected to return to growth in Q1.
Gaming revenue declined 22% sequentially and 11% year on year due to supply constraints.
key_opportunities: Blackwell ramp is the fastest product ramp in company history, with $11 billion of revenue in its first full quarter.
Three scaling laws (pretraining, post-training, inference time scaling) driving demand for AI computing, with reasoning models potentially consuming 100x more compute.
Enterprise revenue grew nearly 2x year on year, with accelerating demand for model fine-tuning, RAG, and agentic AI workflows.
Automotive vertical revenue expected to grow to approximately $5 billion in fiscal 2026.
Networking expected to return to growth in Q1, with Spectrum-X and NVLink Switch as new growth vectors.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management described the Blackwell ramp as 'the fastest product ramp in our company's history, unprecedented in its speed and scale' and expressed confidence in long-term demand drivers, though acknowledged near-term margin and tariff uncertainties.
